patch_description:
This approach replaces the sequential fixed-layer architecture with an adaptive entanglement strategy using alternating basis rotations and varied two-qubit gate types. Instead of global shared phase layers, each qubit gets individualized basis rotations in different bases (RX, RY, RZ in sequence). The entanglement layer uses a mix of CRX, CRY, CRZ with unique parameters (no over-sharing) to maximize expressivity per parameter. Three-qubit gates are placed strategically on diverse qubit triples. This design:
- Reduces generalization gap through less parameter sharing and more diverse connectivity
- Improves test accuracy via better expressivity with fewer parameters
- Maintains computational efficiency with reduced circuit depth
- Enables cleaner gradient flow without redundant shared parameters
The algorithm trades global parameter sharing for local expressivity and diversity, which typically reduces overfitting in quantum classifiers.
